messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-3312345678 — p99 decode latency spike detected in prod (us-west-2).
incident-bot: Auto-page to @sasha, @devon, @mohit. Metric summary: p95 from ~120ms -> 900ms, p99 from ~300ms -> 4.6s. Streaming stalls observed, increased paging/evictions on serving hosts. Auto-run diagnostics attached.

devon: grabbing runtime logs and recent deploys now. I see a kernel update rolled to trt8-kernel-v2 ~18:02 UTC and a compilepath change in the same window.

tara (eng-runtime): confirming, can repro on staging with the same kernel. FlashAttention kernel variant shows higher tail latency under streaming load. Also seeing more ";evict_count" in metrics from the KV cache.

sasha: @devon @tara do we have a quick mitigation? Can we revert the kernel or disable the new flash kernels via runtime flag?

mohit: paging shows constant compilepath misses leading to device memory thrash — GPUs hitting comsat allocator fallback and host-paging. Reverting kernel should be fastest. Rolling back will require a node drain/replace or image rollback depending on how the kernel was delivered.

grace: customer-impact: 3 customers (team-a, retail-search-prod, voice-synthesis) report streaming stalls >10s; overall error rate low but latency SLOs breached for high-throughput chat routes. Escalate for SLA notice if not mitigated in 30m.

devon: Trying a non-invasive mitigation first: set runtime env `REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASH=1` on a canary subset of pods and route 5% of traffic. Command:
```
kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/rt-worker REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASH=1 --record
kubectl -n redwood rollout status deploy/rt-worker-canary
```
If that drops p99, we can widen.

tara (eng-runtime): Also snapshot of `uname -r` on problematic hosts:
```
uname -r
# output: 5.15.89-trt8-v2
```
And decode process logs show repeated compilepath warnings:
```
[decode] compile_path_miss model=redwood-1b quant=8 -> compile_time=0.12s evict=1
[flashattn] init kernel: optimized v2 loaded
```
The combination looks like the new kernel selects flash kernels by default which are slower on long sequences with streaming.

devon: Canary in progress: set env on 4 pods. Initial numbers after 2 minutes: canary p99 dropped from 4.6s -> 480ms, p95 -> 140ms. That's promising.

mohit: Good, that suggests disabling flash kernels helps. While canary widens, I'll prepare node rollback plan: either revert kernel image to trt8-kernel-v1 or deploy a runtime hotfix that forces use of memcpy-based attention kernels.

sasha: @ops-bot can you open a fast-triage ticket and notify infra for a possible kernel rollback? Include affected instance IDs and the time window.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INT-2026-3312. Notifying infra on-call.

grace: Customer comms: I'll draft a targeted note for the 3 impacted customers saying we detected a transient runtime kernel regression, mitigation underway, ETA 30-60m. No data loss. Will post updates every 15m.

devon: Widening canary now to 20% traffic. Monitoring.

(t + 8m) tara (eng-runtime): Canary at 20% shows stable p99 ~520ms, streaming stalls reduced by 92% for the canary routes. Non-canary remains bad. Good candidate mitigation.

mohit: Infra says kernel was shipped as part of image promotion. Rollback of the image is approved but will need staged drain; estimate 4-6 nodes/hr. Alternative: apply runtime patch to force `ATTN_FALLBACK=mem` at runtime which should be faster to roll.

devon: I'll cut a quick runtime patch and push as a config change to all pools (non-disruptive). Patch diff highlights: disable auto-select flashattn for decodes and force fallback when sequence_length > 256. PR: `runtime: disable auto flash attn for streaming`.

tara (eng-runtime): Patch applied to control plane and config propagated. Restarting decoders with zero-downtime rolling restart:
```
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/rt-worker --selector=pool=prod
```
Monitor token-level traces.

(t + 22m) devon: After rollout, overall p99 across prod dropped from 4.6s -> 420ms, p95 back to ~130ms. Streaming stalls are within SLO for chat routes. Eviction rates dropping.

grace: Customer note sent and updated: mitigation applied, monitoring. Will schedule post-mortem with runtime and infra tomorrow.

sasha: Next actions: 1) keep monitoring for 2 hours 2) infra to plan image rollback window for low-traffic block in 6-12h OR validate kernel patches with flashvendor 3) runtime to prepare permanent flag/guardrail in model catalog to prevent auto-selection of flash kernels for streaming workloads.

mohit: I'll own infra rollback plan and coordinate with vendor if needed. Devon/tara please include logs and repro steps in the ticket for vendor triage.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3312345678 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity lowered. Handoff to next oncall in 30m.

sasha: Handoff to @grace for follow-up, I'm signing off from active mitigation.

grace: ACK — I'll own the postmortem and customer follow-up cadence. Will include timeline, root cause (kernel + flashattn auto-selection + compilepath thrash), mitigations, and next steps.

ops-bot: Reminder: please add sla-impact tags and link PRs: INT-2026-3312, PR#6452, CFG#872.

(t + 30m) devon: final note: we should add an automatic runtime gating check: if compilepath evictions > threshold then disable flash kernels automatically. Logged as follow-up CFG-879.

sasha: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem drafted. :thumbsup:
